title: Ground an answer in source text
summary: Grounding means tying an answer to supplied evidence. The answer should stay within what that evidence supports.
introduction: Grounding means tying an answer to supplied evidence. The answer should stay within what that evidence supports. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain ground an answer in source text
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Grounding means tying an answer to supplied evidence. The answer should stay within what that evidence supports.

blocks.code:
Source: The garden club meets on Friday in Room 4.
Task: When does the club meet? Use only the source.
Supported answer: Friday.
blocks.title: Ground an answer in source text

blocks.text: The answer uses the day stated in the source. It does not guess a time because no time appears there.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Ask for the meeting time and write a suitable missing-information answer.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A source can itself be outdated or wrong; grounding helps trace claims but does not prove the source is true.
For more detail later, use this [Generative AI further reading](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/intro-to-ml/what-is-ml).
